events.title: Sun-1 workstation released
events.summary: Sun Microsystems shipped the Sun-1 workstation in May 1982 — a Motorola 68000 machine with bitmapped graphics and Unix for technical computing.
events.about: Sun workstations ran BSD Unix on affordable hardware with networking built in — NFS, RPC, and later Java were born in this ecosystem. Developers at startups, universities, and Wall Street traded green-screen terminals for networked bitmap displays. Sun's "the network is the computer" slogan described how backend devs actually worked.

narrative.whyChosen: Sun-1 launched the Unix workstation market that powered the 1980s–90s internet buildout.
narrative.whyImportant: It paired open Unix with commodity hardware — a model Linux servers later scaled globally.
narrative.problemSolved: Engineers needed interactive graphics and Unix on a desk without million-dollar minicomputers.
